scope: Theorem 9.3 (Phase alternative) of the manuscript “A counterexample to the Colin de Verdière chromatic conjecture” (preprints/A-counterexample-to-the-Colin-de-Verdiere-chromatic-conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 157 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 97677c7a183884f0), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 59. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose a marked-unit law σ satisfies σi ≤ Λπ (i = 1, 2), σ ≤ 2(D+.01)N P0 2 , where Λ is fixed before the channel size, and suppose ∆O ̸= 0 throughout. For all sufficiently large n, one can retain a sublaw of relative mass at least δph > 0, depending only on the early parameters, such that one of the following holds for independent draws A, B: (i) every nontrivial phase mean E(−1)uB,S(∆A)+uA,R(∆B) , (S, R) ̸= (∅, ∅), has absolute value less than .005; (ii) writing F(A, B) = uB,{1,2}(∆A), one has F(A, B) = 0 for every pair of retained units, and every displayed mean for which |S| = 1 or |R| = 1 is 2−Ω(N). All marks remain in their first effective spaces. No additional image directions are pinned. Neither the retained-mass bound nor the tiny-cover dimension used in the proof depends on selector or channel sizes; the lower bound required of h may depend on Λ.
